thesis: The speaker defines being human as the unique ability to contribute to a knowledge loop by recording and sharing knowledge artifacts over time and space, a capability that will persist even as machines become capable of participating in that loop. He suggests that in a future with augmented humans and machine neo-humans, humans will still be valued for their qualia, which is the subjective feeling of experience that machines cannot yet replicate.
